findings.issue_text: Blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts:68-77 lowercases env entries but compares the raw non-lowercased guest email, so BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is trivially bypassed by varying email case (e.g. Banned@Example.com), allowing blocked addresses to be added as attendees and emailed

EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts:153-161 is constructed from the requesting session user instead of the booking organizer, so when a team admin/owner or attendee adds guests the calendar attendee update runs against the wrong user's credentials and silently no-ops or fails; the organizer's external calendar event never gets the new guests and booking.user.credentials from the include are never used

isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts:44-46 uses && (requiring the user to be both admin AND owner) despite the name and intent being OR, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN

The evt: CalendarEvent in addGuests.handler.ts:119-142 never sets team, so in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:529-535) calendarEvent.team?.members is always undefined: the team-member notification loop is dead code, team members are never emailed, and the attendee email subject falls back to the organizer name instead of the team name for team bookings

Attendees are persisted via prisma.booking.update before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees with no try/catch or rollback in addGuests.handler.ts:91-161; if the calendar update throws, the mutation errors even though guests were already written to the DB, and a user retry then hits the duplicate-email rejection path, leaving inconsistent state

No booking status/time validation in addGuests.handler.ts:26-42: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, and every recipient is sent an ICS with status CONFIRMED for an event that isn't happening

Duplicate detection guest === attendee.email in addGuests.handler.ts:73-74 is case-sensitive though emails are case-insensitive, so User@Example.com passes when user@example.com is already an attendee, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

The server schema in addGuests.schema.ts:5-7 omits the uniqueness .refine() that the client applies (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-30), so a direct API call can submit duplicate emails in one request and createMany will create duplicate attendee rows; uniqueness is enforced only client-side

No .max() bound on the guests array in addGuests.schema.ts:6, so a single authorized request can create thousands of attendee rows and trigger unbounded email fan-out (each add emails all existing attendees plus organizer/team), an easy mail-bombing/DoS vector for an authenticated user

Check-then-act on attendees with no transaction or DB-level uniqueness guarantee in addGuests.handler.ts:72-101: two concurrent addGuests requests can both read the same attendee list, both pass the dedupe filter, and both createMany, producing duplicate attendees

No tests added for the new addGuests handler (permission matrix incl. admin/owner logic, dedupe, blacklist), the input schema, AddGuestsDialog, or the new MultiEmail component, despite the handler containing authorization and data-mutation logic

catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") } in addGuests.handler.ts:163-167 discards the error object (no details, no logger), making email delivery failures completely undiagnosable in production

AddGuestsDialog.tsx dialog state is only reset by the Cancel button: closing via onOpenChange (overlay/Esc) leaves multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail stale, and isInvalidEmail is never cleared when the user edits inputs or on success, so reopening shows stale emails and a lingering 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner

showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests")) in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-44: message is always a non-empty template string so the fallback is unreachable, and err.data?.code renders as literal 'undefined' when absent, producing toasts like 'undefined: ...'

prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) in addGuests.handler.ts:56-58 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error (surfaced as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) when booking.userId is null, instead of a handled TRPCError

New guests are persisted with name: "" in addGuests.handler.ts:83-90, so emails are addressed as " <email>", attendee records/ICS carry empty CN values, and the organizer subject line (this.calEvent.attendees[0].name) can render a blank name since attendee ordering is unspecified
The 'Remove email' tooltip text in MultiEmail.tsx:38 is hardcoded English while the rest of the component uses t(), so it won't be localized

The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS environment variable consumed in addGuests.handler.ts:68-71 has no documentation added in this PR (.env.example / docs), leaving the operator-facing control undiscoverable

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts:153-161 is constructed from the requesting session user instead of the booking organizer, so when a team admin/owner or attendee adds guests the calendar attendee update runs against the wrong user's credentials and silently no-ops or fails; the organizer's external calendar event never gets the new guests and booking.user.credentials from the include are never used

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler builds the `EventManager` from the requesting session user (`const { user } = ctx;` then `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`). This is independent of the booking organizer (`organizer` is fetched separately and `booking.user.credentials` is included in the initial booking query but never used). Therefore, if a team admin/owner or an attendee (not the organizer) calls `addGuests`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can prevent updating the organizer’s external calendar event correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts:44-46 uses && (requiring the user to be both admin AND owner) despite the name and intent being OR, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && in isTeamAdminOrOwner requires a user to be both admin and owner, but the intended behavior is admin OR owner, leading to incorrect FORBIDDEN responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The evt: CalendarEvent in addGuests.handler.ts:119-142 never sets team, so in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:529-535) calendarEvent.team?.members is always undefined: the team-member notification loop is dead code, team members are never emailed, and the attendee email subject falls back to the organizer name instead of the team name for team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes organizer/attendees/etc. but never sets any `team` field (nor does the booking query include loading the team/members). Yet `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts) relies on `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify team members and uses `calendarEvent.team?.name` in the attendee email subject fallback. From what’s shown in the diff, `calendarEvent.team` will always be undefined for team bookings, making the team-member notification loop effectively unreachable and causing subject/name fallback to use the organizer name instead of the team name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are persisted via prisma.booking.update before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees with no try/catch or rollback in addGuests.handler.ts:91-161; if the calendar update throws, the mutation errors even though guests were already written to the DB, and a user retry then hits the duplicate-email rejection path, leaving inconsistent state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation writes new attendees to the DB first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or transactional rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the handler will error while the DB changes have already been committed. A subsequent retry will compute `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees`, resulting in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and a BAD_REQUEST (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), matching the inconsistent-state scenario described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status/time validation in addGuests.handler.ts:26-42: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, and every recipient is sent an ICS with status CONFIRMED for an event that isn't happening

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler loads the booking by `id` and proceeds to update `attendees` and send notifications without checking any booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or whether `startTime/endTime` are in the past (no validation after the `findFirst` at the top of the handler). Separately, the newly added email templates always generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if this mutation is invoked on a non-active booking, recipients can receive a CONFIRMED calendar update for something that may no longer be happening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate detection guest === attendee.email in addGuests.handler.ts:73-74 is case-sensitive though emails are case-insensitive, so User@Example.com passes when user@example.com is already an attendee, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a case-sensitive comparison `guest === attendee.email` (and blacklist check compares lowercased blacklist entries against the raw `guest`). Since emails are generally treated as case-insensitive identifiers, this allows adding `User@Example.com` even if `user@example.com` is already an attendee, leading to duplicate attendee rows and duplicate notifications/calendar updates. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) before the duplicate check or insert.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The server schema in addGuests.schema.ts:5-7 omits the uniqueness .refine() that the client applies (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-30), so a direct API call can submit duplicate emails in one request and createMany will create duplicate attendee rows; uniqueness is enforced only client-side
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: duplicate emails within a single add-guests request are not deduplicated/validated server-side, so createMany can insert multiple attendee rows for the same email if the client submits repeats. The candidate frames it as missing server-side uniqueness validation (only enforced client-side), which is consistent with the golden issue’s effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No .max() bound on the guests array in addGuests.schema.ts:6, so a single authorized request can create thousands of attendee rows and trigger unbounded email fan-out (each add emails all existing attendees plus organizer/team), an easy mail-bombing/DoS vector for an authenticated user

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new authed TRPC mutation `addGuests` that accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`). The handler then blindly `createMany` attendee rows for the provided emails (`addGuests.handler.ts`), and triggers email fan-out via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends organizer/team emails plus one email per attendee (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`). With no `.max()` (or other server-side limit), an authenticated caller who is permitted (organizer/attendee/admin/owner) could submit a very large array to create many rows and trigger large email sends, i.e., a practical DoS/mail-bombing vector visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-act on attendees with no transaction or DB-level uniqueness guarantee in addGuests.handler.ts:72-101: two concurrent addGuests requests can both read the same attendee list, both pass the dedupe filter, and both createMany, producing duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first reads existing attendees (booking.findFirst include attendees) then computes uniqueGuests by filtering against that snapshot, and finally does booking.update with attendees.createMany. There is no transaction/locking and no Prisma createMany skipDuplicates flag, so two concurrent addGuests calls can both pass the filter and both insert the same guest email(s), creating duplicates (or causing a uniqueness error if a DB constraint exists, which is not shown in the diff). This is a real race introduced by the new handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for the new addGuests handler (permission matrix incl. admin/owner logic, dedupe, blacklist), the input schema, AddGuestsDialog, or the new MultiEmail component, despite the handler containing authorization and data-mutation logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` with auth checks and DB mutation in `addGuests.handler.ts`, new zod schema `addGuests.schema.ts`, new UI dialog `AddGuestsDialog`, and new reusable `MultiEmail` component exported from `@calcom/ui`) but the diff does not include any corresponding test additions (no new/modified test files are shown). Given the handler includes permission logic, attendee dedupe/blacklist filtering, and a `prisma.booking.update` mutation plus side effects (calendar update + email sending), the lack of tests for these code paths is a concrete, diff-grounded review gap rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") } in addGuests.handler.ts:163-167 discards the error object (no details, no logger), making email delivery failures completely undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the thrown error and logs no `err` details (stack/message) and uses `console.log` instead of a structured logger. This doesn’t break core functionality (guests are still added and calendar attendees updated), but it makes production email failures hard to debug and is directly grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx dialog state is only reset by the Cancel button: closing via onOpenChange (overlay/Esc) leaves multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail stale, and isInvalidEmail is never cleared when the user edits inputs or on success, so reopening shows stale emails and a lingering 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, dialog open/close is controlled by `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>`, but there is no effect/handler to reset `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail` when the dialog is closed via overlay click/Esc (i.e., through `onOpenChange`). Reset only happens on the Cancel button click (clears both) and partially on mutation success (clears `multiEmailValue` but does not clear `isInvalidEmail`). Also, `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on validation failure and is never cleared when the user edits `MultiEmail` inputs (`setMultiEmailValue` is called without resetting `isInvalidEmail`), so the error banner can persist after correcting input and/or across reopenings if the dialog was closed without pressing Cancel.

adjudication_records.issue_text: showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests")) in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-44: message is always a non-empty template string so the fallback is unreachable, and err.data?.code renders as literal 'undefined' when absent, producing toasts like 'undefined: ...'

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `message` as a template string: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template string is always a non-empty string, even when `err.data?.code` is missing (it becomes the literal text `"undefined"`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never use the fallback and can display toasts like `"undefined: ..."`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) in addGuests.handler.ts:56-58 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error (surfaced as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) when booking.userId is null, instead of a handled TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The preceding booking lookup (`prisma.booking.findFirst`) does not enforce `userId` to be non-null, and later logic allows non-organizer users (e.g., an attendee) to proceed. If `booking.userId` is `null`, this code will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma not-found), which is not converted into a `TRPCError` anywhere in this handler, plausibly surfacing as an internal server error instead of a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests are persisted with name: "" in addGuests.handler.ts:83-90, so emails are addressed as " <email>", attendee records/ICS carry empty CN values, and the organizer subject line (this.calEvent.attendees[0].name) can render a blank name since attendee ordering is unspecified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly created attendee records are persisted with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails` mapping). Those records are then used to build `attendeesList` (name taken directly from DB), which is passed into `CalendarEvent` and downstream emails/ICS generation. The Node email template `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` formats the recipient as `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`, which will render as ` <email>` when `name` is empty. Additionally, `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` for the subject `name`, and since attendee ordering from `include: { attendees: true }` is not specified in the diff, `attendees[0]` can be one of the newly added blank-name guests, resulting in a blank name in the subject.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'Remove email' tooltip text in MultiEmail.tsx:38 is hardcoded English while the rest of the component uses t(), so it won't be localized

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the tooltip is `content="Remove email"` (hardcoded English) while the component otherwise uses `useLocale().t()` for user-facing strings (e.g., the "add_another" button label). This means that tooltip text will not be localized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS environment variable consumed in addGuests.handler.ts:68-71 has no documentation added in this PR (.env.example / docs), leaving the operator-facing control undiscoverable

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new operator-controlled env var `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` in `addGuests.handler.ts` (used to filter `uniqueGuests`), but this PR does not add any corresponding documentation or example configuration (no `.env.example`/docs changes appear in the provided diff). That makes the new control undiscoverable to operators, but it’s not a runtime correctness defect by itself.
